predecessors.name: Akkadian Empire
predecessors.text: the city of Mari and its surroundings, the seat of the Akkadian-appointed Shakkanakku (a 60 km disc around Tell Hariri)

successors.name: Lim dynasty of Mari
successors.text: the Euphrates around Mari that the Lim dynasty takes as its seat c.

ledger.x: 2266 BCE: Ididish, the first Shakkanakku on the lists, governs a restored Mari for Akkad.
2217 BCE: Mari becomes independent as Akkad disintegrates.
1830 BCE: the Shakkanakku state ends and the Euphrates outside the Lim seat is left unattributed.
1830 BCE: the Shakkanakku dynasty gives way to the Amorite Lim dynasty at Mari. the page says that around 1830 BC Mari became the seat of the Amorite Lim dynasty under Yaggid-Lim; by c.

certainty.note: The page gives no territory for the Shakkanakku state; the middle Euphrates is the researcher's reading, and the Ur III periphery had 'fluctuating boundaries'.
